newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Clariant shoots for 15 pct return on sales.
newsitem.headline: Clariant shoots for 15 pct return on sales.

text.p: Clariant AG chief executive Rolf Schweizer said the revamped group aimed to boost operating profit to 15 percent of sales by the year 2000 and could make new acquisitions to round out its specialty chemicals business.

"We are homing in on sales in the magnitude of 10 billion Swiss francs at the turn of the millennium. Operating profit should reach 15 percent of sales, so profitability will rise strongly," he told the Finanz und Wirtschaft newspaper in an interview published on Wednesday.
Clariant is getting the speciality chemical business of Hoechst AG under a merger announced on Tuesday.
He said the integration process would be concluded in the second half of 1998 and would save the company around 500 million francs in costs.

"Afterwards -- and in part even before then -- we will optimise the entire group's portfolio, which means selling areas that don't fit, bringing them into joint ventures or swapping them with other companies. Acquisitions to round things out are also possible," he said.
He said it was too soon to say how much the deal would cost Clariant because the Hoechst specialty chemicals business was still being valued.

Schweizer said Hoechst was only getting a minority stake in the revamped group because Clariant insisted on remaining independent. "This is why it was agreed that Hoechst could transfer debt to Clariant as additional compensation."

He said Hoechst had already spent lots of money to reationalise the business, so the group should be able to exploit synergies immediately by combining production and sales and merging the companies' know-how.
He hoped cartel authorities would not object to the two companies' strong master batch positions because it was too difficult to dominate the market. -- Zurich +41 1 631 7340
